4 انهضهُ He made him, or excited him, to rise, or stand up. (S, A, * K, TA:) or he roused him. or put him in portion to rise. (TA.) You say also, لِلْأَمْرِ ↓ إِنْتَهَضْتُهُ , [if this be not a mistranscription for ??,] I made him to rise to (do, or perform,] the affair. (Msb,) And انهضهُ عَلَى الشَّىْءِ (assumed tropical:) He strengthened him to rise, and do, or perform, the thing. (TA.) ―
-b2- انهض القِرْبَةَ: He nearly filled the water-skin [so as to make it rise]. (K. TA.) ―
-b3- أَنْهَضَتِ الرِّيحُ السَّحَابَ (tropical:) The wind bore and drove along the cloud, or clouds. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
